Definition: from G1725; opposite; figuratively, antagonistic:--(over) against, contrary.
BiblicalUsage: Enantios is what stands opposite — contrary, against. The wind was contrary to the disciples as they rowed in Mark 6:48 and Matthew 14:24, Paul once thought he ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus in Acts 26:9, and Paul says the persecutors are contrary to all men in 1 Thessalonians 2:15.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe contrary winds are part of the voyage — the disciples rowed against the wind all night and Jesus still came walking to them on the sea. I hold that opposition does not mean God has left us; often it is the very place where He shows up.
